name: New Zealand

facts.languages: English, Māori, New Zealand Sign Language

snapshot: Christopher Luxon's centre-right coalition faces voters on 7 November 2026, after a term of spending cuts and fights over the Treaty of Waitangi.
culture: Māori culture is central to national identity: the haka, performed by the All Blacks before matches, te reo Māori, now widely used in public life, and marae, community meeting grounds. Rugby is a national passion. The landscapes that starred in "The Lord of the Rings" drive tourism.
society: Dairy, meat and wine exports and tourism drive the economy. The Treaty of Waitangi, signed in 1840 between the Crown and Māori chiefs, shapes law and politics; a 2024 bill to redefine it sparked a huge hīkoi protest march. Housing is expensive, and many young people move to Australia.
situation: New Zealand was once the place Australians and Britons imagined escaping to. In 2025 a record number of New Zealanders left for Australia and elsewhere instead, a fact Labour's leader seized on as a verdict on the country's economy (AAP). The country's 2026 was one long election campaign shaped by that mood.

Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, a former Air New Zealand chief executive, announced in January that the election would be held on 7 November, unusually late, which his opponent called a sign of desperation (1News). It is a rematch of 2023 with the roles reversed: Luxon defends a conservative coalition with the libertarian ACT and Winston Peters's populist New Zealand First, while Labour's Chris Hipkins, who briefly succeeded Jacinda Ardern, tries to return. The backdrop is grim for an incumbent. The economy contracted in three of six quarters, unemployment hit a nine-year high of 5.3 percent, and Luxon has the worst net popularity of any first-term prime minister in recent memory (AP via ClickOrlando). Yet New Zealand rarely throws out a government after one term, and polls show the two blocs close, with the Greens and Te Pāti Māori Labour's likely partners. The vote is four weeks away.
power: A parliamentary democracy and Commonwealth realm with no written constitution. The prime minister leads the government with a majority in the single-chamber House of Representatives, about 120 seats elected by mixed-member proportional representation, so coalitions are the norm. Elections are held every three years.
holders: Prime Minister Christopher Luxon (National), with ACT and New Zealand First.
